claim: Therapeutic targeting of Mir221/222 in specific SF subpopulations could lead to novel fibroblast-targeted therapies.
source: Our results establish an SF-specific pathogenic role of Mir221/222 in arthritis and suggest that its therapeutic targeting in specific subpopulations could lead to novel fibroblast-targeted therapies.
evidence: This claim is speculative based on the results presented in the manuscript.

claim: Genetically modified mouse models with deregulated expression of TNF develop an erosive polyarthritis resembling RA.
source: Genetically modified mouse models with deregulated expression of TNF develop an erosive polyarthritis resembling RA (huTNFtg) (Keffer et al., 1991) and SpAs (spondyloarthropathies) (TNFΔARE [Kontoyiannis et al., 1999], TgA86 [Küsters et al., 1997; Vafeiadou et al., 2020]), showing also extra-articular manifestations, such as heart valve disease and intestinal inflammation, recapitulating comorbid pathologies often observed in humans (Kontoyiannis et al., 1999; Ntari et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: TNF targeting of TNFR1 on synovial fibroblasts is required for the development of arthritis.
source: Early studies in our lab established that TNF targeting of TNFR1 on synovial fibroblasts (SFs) is required for the development of arthritis and suffices to orchestrate full pathogenesis (Armaka et al., 2008; Armaka et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies from the authors' lab.

claim: TNF targeting of TNFR1 on synovial fibroblasts suffices to orchestrate full pathogenesis.
source: Early studies in our lab established that TNF targeting of TNFR1 on synovial fibroblasts (SFs) is required for the development of arthritis and suffices to orchestrate full pathogenesis (Armaka et al., 2008; Armaka et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies from the authors' lab.

claim: Under chronic inflammatory signals, SFs hyperproliferate.
source: Under chronic inflammatory signals, SFs hyperproliferate, express ECM-degrading enzymes, and acquire an aggressive, invasive, and tissue-destructive phenotype (Kontoyiannis and Kollias, 2000; Dakin et al., 2018; Koliaraki et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Under chronic inflammatory signals, SFs express ECM-degrading enzymes.
source: Under chronic inflammatory signals, SFs hyperproliferate, express ECM-degrading enzymes, and acquire an aggressive, invasive, and tissue-destructive phenotype (Kontoyiannis and Kollias, 2000; Dakin et al., 2018; Koliaraki et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Under chronic inflammatory signals, SFs acquire an aggressive, invasive, and tissue-destructive phenotype.
source: Under chronic inflammatory signals, SFs hyperproliferate, express ECM-degrading enzymes, and acquire an aggressive, invasive, and tissue-destructive phenotype (Kontoyiannis and Kollias, 2000; Dakin et al., 2018; Koliaraki et al., 2020).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Arthritogenic SFs can migrate via the circulation to distant sites and transfer disease in both mice and humans.
source: In addition, arthritogenic SFs can migrate via the circulation to distant sites and transfer disease in both mice and humans (Aidinis et al., 2003; Lefèvre et al., 2009).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Epigenetic alterations, such as global DNA hypomethylation and deregulated expression of miRNAs and lncRNAs, have been linked to the aggressive and destructive behavior of SFs.
source: Epigenetic alterations, such as global DNA hypomethylation and deregulated expression of miRNAs and lncRNAs (Karouzakis et al., 2009; Evangelatos et al., 2019; Zou et al., 2018), have been linked to the aggressive and destructive behavior of SFs.
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mir221 and Mir222 have been found upregulated in SFs derived from the huTNFtg mouse model and RA patients.
source: Specifically, Mir221 and Mir222 have been found upregulated in SFs derived from the huTNFtg mouse model and RA patients (Pandis et al., 2012).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Mir221/222 are clustered on the X chromosome (Mirc53 locus).
source: Mir221/222 are clustered on the X chromosome (Mirc53 locus) and classified as oncomiRs as they are upregulated in a number of human epithelial cancers.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Mir221/222 are classified as oncomiRs as they are upregulated in a number of human epithelial cancers.
source: Mir221/222 are clustered on the X chromosome (Mirc53 locus) and classified as oncomiRs as they are upregulated in a number of human epithelial cancers.
evidence: This claim is based on established scientific knowledge.

claim: Mir221/222 target genes mainly involved in cell proliferation and survival, such as cell cycle inhibitors Cdkn1b and Cdkn1c.
source: They target genes mainly involved in cell proliferation and survival, such as cell cycle inhibitors Cdkn1b and Cdkn1c (le Sage et al., 2007; Pineau et al., 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Under nonresolving inflammatory signals, such as in sepsis, the overexpression of Mir222 contributes to morbidity by targeting Smarca4.
source: Under nonresolving inflammatory signals, such as in sepsis, the overexpression of Mir222 contributes to morbidity by targeting Smarca4, a chromatin remodeling component that participates in the SWI/SNF complex (Seeley et al., 2018).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Expression levels of Mir221/222 positively correlate with disease progression in RA.
source: In RA, expression levels of Mir221/222 positively correlate with disease progression (Abo ElAtta et al., 2019) and ex vivo downregulation of Mir221 has been shown to decrease migration and invasion of human RA SFs (Yang and Yang, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Ex vivo downregulation of Mir221 has been shown to decrease migration and invasion of human RA SFs.
source: In RA, expression levels of Mir221/222 positively correlate with disease progression (Abo ElAtta et al., 2019) and ex vivo downregulation of Mir221 has been shown to decrease migration and invasion of human RA SFs (Yang and Yang, 2015).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study.

claim: Both Mir221 and Mir222 were upregulated from the early disease stage in huTNFtg mice.
source: Both Mir221 and Mir222 were upregulated from the early disease stage, and this upregulation was further augmented with disease progression (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Mir221 and Mir222 upregulation was further augmented with disease progression in huTNFtg mice.
source: Both Mir221 and Mir222 were upregulated from the early disease stage, and this upregulation was further augmented with disease progression (Figure 1A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1A and B.

claim: Mir221/222 expression is induced by LPS and TNF in macrophages.
source: Previous studies have shown that Mir221/222 expression is induced by LPS and TNF in macrophages and that they are implicated in LPS tolerance and endotoxemia (Seeley et al., 2018; El Gazzar and McCall, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: Mir221/222 are implicated in LPS tolerance and endotoxemia.
source: Previous studies have shown that Mir221/222 expression is induced by LPS and TNF in macrophages and that they are implicated in LPS tolerance and endotoxemia (Seeley et al., 2018; El Gazzar and McCall, 2010).
evidence: This claim is supported by citations to previous studies.

claim: TNF led to consistent upregulation of both Mir221 and Mir222 in SFs at all time points examined.
source: TNF, LPS, and IL-1β led to consistent upregulation of both Mir221 and Mir222 in SFs at all time points examined (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: LPS led to consistent upregulation of both Mir221 and Mir222 in SFs at all time points examined.
source: TNF, LPS, and IL-1β led to consistent upregulation of both Mir221 and Mir222 in SFs at all time points examined (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: IL-1β led to consistent upregulation of both Mir221 and Mir222 in SFs at all time points examined.
source: TNF, LPS, and IL-1β led to consistent upregulation of both Mir221 and Mir222 in SFs at all time points examined (Figure 1C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1C and D.

claim: Mir221/222 were found not to be induced in the absence of TNFR1 in huTNFtg mice.
source: These mice do not develop any RA pathology and the two miRNAs were found not to be induced in the absence of TNFR1 (Figure 1E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1E and F.

claim: Anakinra did not abrogate Mir221/222 induction by TNF.
source: Anakinra successfully inhibited downstream IL-1β signaling (Figure 1—figure supplement 1C), but did not abrogate Mir221/222 induction by TNF (Figure 1G and H).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 1G and H.

claim: TNF may upregulate Mir221/222 independently of IL-1β.
source: Thus, TNF may upregulate Mir221/222 independently of IL-1β.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing that anakinra did not block TNF-induced Mir221/222 expression.

claim: Histopathological analysis revealed exacerbated arthritis in huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice compared to huTNFtg controls.
source: Histopathological analysis revealed exacerbated arthritis, as observed by enhanced synovial hyperplasia (pannus formation), cartilage destruction, and number of osteoclasts in the double huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 transgenic mice in comparison to the huTNFtg controls (Figure 2B).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2B.

claim: Bone morphometric analysis using microCT revealed greater bone erosions in huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice.
source: Moreover, bone morphometric analysis using microCT revealed greater bone erosions as indicated by decreased bone volume, decreased trabecular thickness, and increased trabecular separation (Figure 2C–F).
evidence: This claim is supported by microCT data shown in Figure 2C-F.

claim: Comparison of TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 to WT mice revealed significantly decreased trabecular thickness.
source: Interestingly, comparison of TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 to WT mice revealed significantly decreased trabecular thickness, as well as a tendency for decreased bone volume and increased trabecular separation (Figure 2D–F, Figure 2—figure supplement 2A), suggesting a potential a priori function of the two miRNAs in bone physiology, which needs further elucidation.
evidence: This claim is supported by microCT data shown in Figure 2D-F and Figure 2—figure supplement 2A.

claim: huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222;Mir221/222-/- mice exhibited synovial hyperplasia, cartilage destruction, and number of osteoclasts as the huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222;Mir221/222 d/f, f/- mice.
source: huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222;Mir221/222-/- mice exhibited synovial hyperplasia, cartilage destruction, and number of osteoclasts as the huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222;Mir221/222 d/f, f/- mice (Figure 2G), indicating that SF-specific Mir221/222 overexpression even in the absence of Mir221/222 in other cell types is sufficient to deteriorate arthritis manifestations.
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: SF-specific Mir221/222 overexpression even in the absence of Mir221/222 in other cell types is sufficient to deteriorate arthritis manifestations.
source: huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222;Mir221/222-/- mice exhibited synovial hyperplasia, cartilage destruction, and number of osteoclasts as the huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222;Mir221/222 d/f, f/- mice (Figure 2G), indicating that SF-specific Mir221/222 overexpression even in the absence of Mir221/222 in other cell types is sufficient to deteriorate arthritis manifestations.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data shown in Figure 2G.

claim: Mir221/222 overexpression did not lead to a significant increase in inflammatory infiltrations, apart from an increase in CD8+ T cells.
source: Next, we checked the role of Mir221/222 overexpression in immune infiltration in the joints of huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice and observed that it did not lead to a significant increase in inflammatory infiltrations, apart from an increase in CD8+ T cells (Figure 3A, Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B) compared to huTNFtg mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 3A and Figure 3—figure supplement 1A and B.

claim: Effector CD8+ T cells were the predominant CD8+ T cell subpopulation in the arthritic joints.
source: CD8+ T cell subpopulations were further characterized and effector CD8+ T cells were found to be the predominant CD8+ T cell subpopulation in the arthritic joints.
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Effector CD8+ T cells were increased in the joints of huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 compared to the huTNFtg mice.
source: Moreover, effector CD8+ T cells were increased in the joints of huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 compared to the huTNFtg mice and accounted for the observed increase in CD8+ T cells (Figure 3—figure supplement 1B, Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1B and Figure 3—figure supplement 2A–D.

claim: Both lining layer SFs (LLSFs) and sublining layer SFs (SLSFs) were expanded in huTNFtg mice compared to WT.
source: Similar to human RA, both lining layer SFs (LLSFs) and sublining layer SFs (SLSFs) were expanded in huTNFtg mice compared to WT, as indicated by FACS analysis (Figure 3B, Figure 3—figure supplement 1C).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 3B and Figure 3—figure supplement 1C.

claim: Mir221/222 overexpression in arthritis rendered both lining and sublining layers more hyperplastic in huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice compared to huTNFtg.
source: Notably, Mir221/222 overexpression in arthritis rendered both layers more hyperplastic in huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice compared to huTNFtg.
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mir221/222 overexpression alone was sufficient to increase the number of fibroblasts of the LL and SL in TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice.
source: It is worth mentioning that Mir221/222 overexpression alone was sufficient to increase the number of fibroblasts of the LL and SL in TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice (Figure 3B).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 3B.

claim: An increase in Mir221/222 levels was observed, mainly, in fibroblasts of the LL and to a lesser extent in those of the SL.
source: An increase in Mir221/222 levels was observed, mainly, in fibroblasts of the LL and to a lesser extent in those of the SL (Figure 3C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 3C and D.

claim: Both WT and huTNFtg SFs overexpressing Mir221/222 exhibited increased proliferation compared to their respective controls.
source: In agreement with the in vivo data, both WT and huTNFtg SFs overexpressing Mir221/222 exhibited increased proliferation and wound-healing potential compared to their respective controls (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 3E.

claim: Both WT and huTNFtg SFs overexpressing Mir221/222 exhibited increased wound-healing potential compared to their respective controls.
source: In agreement with the in vivo data, both WT and huTNFtg SFs overexpressing Mir221/222 exhibited increased proliferation and wound-healing potential compared to their respective controls (Figure 3E and F).
evidence: This claim is supported by wound-healing assay data shown in Figure 3F.

claim: KEGG pathway analysis of significantly differentially expressed genes showed strong over-representation of pathways involved in cell cycle and DNA replication in the group of upregulated genes.
source: KEGG pathway analysis of significantly differentially expressed genes showed strong over-representation of pathways involved in cell cycle and DNA replication in the group of upregulated genes, while functional terms such as ECM function and AKT signaling were enriched among the downregulated ones (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: Functional terms such as ECM function and AKT signaling were enriched among the downregulated genes.
source: KEGG pathway analysis of significantly differentially expressed genes showed strong over-representation of pathways involved in cell cycle and DNA replication in the group of upregulated genes, while functional terms such as ECM function and AKT signaling were enriched among the downregulated ones (Figure 4A).
evidence: This claim is supported by KEGG pathway analysis shown in Figure 4A.

claim: All Cdkn1b, Cdkn1c, and Smarca1 were found to be downregulated in SFs from huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice compared to huTNFtg mice both at the RNA and protein levels.
source: All Cdkn1b, Cdkn1c, and Smarca1 were found to be downregulated in SFs from huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice compared to huTNFtg mice both at the RNA and protein levels (Figure 4C–E and H–L).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR and western blot data shown in Figure 4C–E and H–L.

claim: Mir222/221 target specific cell cycle inhibitors (Cdkn1b and Cdkn1c) in order to induce proliferation of fibroblasts.
source: Together our data suggest that Mir222/221 target specific cell cycle inhibitors (Cdkn1b and Cdkn1c) in order to induce proliferation of fibroblasts.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing downregulation of Cdkn1b and Cdkn1c and increased proliferation.

claim: Smarca1 is a novel Mir221/222 target involved in chromatin dynamics.
source: Additionally, we also identified Smarca1, a novel Mir221/222 target involved in chromatin dynamics.
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental validation data presented in the manuscript.

claim: ECM-related genes such as Prg4 and Itga3 were found to be downregulated in huTNFtg SFs.
source: ECM-related genes such as Prg4 and Itga3 were found to be downregulated in huTNFtg SFs.
evidence: This claim is supported by RNA-seq data presented in the manuscript.

claim: Mir221/222 overexpression resulted in enhanced downregulation of Prg4 and Itga3.
source: Interestingly, Mir221/222 overexpression resulted in enhanced downregulation of these genes, probably through indirect mechanisms as they were not predicted to be direct targets (Figure 4F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4F and G.

claim: No difference was observed in Mmp3 and Rankl levels in arthritogenic SFs due to Mir221/222 overexpression.
source: However, no difference was observed in Mmp3 and Rankl levels in arthritogenic SFs due to Mir221/222 overexpression (Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2A and B.

claim: No changes were observed in IL-6 protein levels in supernatants of naïve or TNF stimulated SFs from Mir221/222 overexpressing mice.
source: We did not observe any changes neither in the IL-6 protein levels in supernatants of naïve or TNF stimulated SFs nor in Il6 RNA levels in SFs from Mir221/222 overexpressing mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2C.

claim: No changes were observed in Il6 RNA levels in SFs from Mir221/222 overexpressing mice.
source: We did not observe any changes neither in the IL-6 protein levels in supernatants of naïve or TNF stimulated SFs nor in Il6 RNA levels in SFs from Mir221/222 overexpressing mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2C and D).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2D.

claim: RNA levels of TNF were not altered in SFs from huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice compared to huTNFtg.
source: RNA levels of TNF were not altered in SFs from huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice compared to huTNFtg (Figure 4—figure supplement 2E).
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2E.

claim: No difference in the levels of human TNF and no mouse TNF protein was detected in the sera or supernatants of cultured SFs from huTNFtg and huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice.
source: Moreover, no difference in the levels of human TNF and no mouse TNF protein was detected in the sera or supernatants of cultured SFs from huTNFtg and huTNFtg;TgCol6a1-Mir221/222 mice (Figure 4—figure supplement 2F and G).
evidence: This claim is supported by ELISA data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2F and G.

claim: No differences were observed in ICAM-1 and VCAM-1 expression due to Mir221/222 overexpression.
source: To examine whether Mir221/222 overexpression rendered fibroblasts more activated, we measured the expression of activation markers, such as ICAM-1 and VCAM-1, but no differences were observed (Figure 4—figure supplement 2H1).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 4—figure supplement 2H and I.

claim: Mir221/222 overexpression shifts the gene expression of arthritogenic SFs to a more proliferative and less ECM-producing signature.
source: It is therefore evident that Mir221/222 overexpression shifts the gene expression of arthritogenic SFs to a more proliferative and less ECM-producing signature, without any evidence of switching to a more pro-inflammatory or activated state.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data presented in the manuscript.

claim: huTNFtg;Mir221/222-/- mice presented with decreased synovial hyperplasia compared to huTNFtg.
source: huTNFtg;Mir221/222-/- mice presented with decreased synovial hyperplasia, cartilage destruction, and number of osteoclasts, as seen in histological analysis, compared to huTNFtg (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: huTNFtg;Mir221/222-/- mice presented with decreased cartilage destruction compared to huTNFtg.
source: huTNFtg;Mir221/222-/- mice presented with decreased synovial hyperplasia, cartilage destruction, and number of osteoclasts, as seen in histological analysis, compared to huTNFtg (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: huTNFtg;Mir221/222-/- mice presented with decreased number of osteoclasts compared to huTNFtg.
source: huTNFtg;Mir221/222-/- mice presented with decreased synovial hyperplasia, cartilage destruction, and number of osteoclasts, as seen in histological analysis, compared to huTNFtg (Figure 5A).
evidence: This claim is supported by histological data shown in Figure 5A.

claim: Mir221/222 deletion in arthritis did not alter the inflammatory influx.
source: Additionally, Mir221/222 deletion in arthritis did not alter the inflammatory influx (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), but rather led to the inhibition of fibroblast expansion of LL and SL in the joints (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 5—figure supplement 1.

claim: Mir221/222 deletion led to the inhibition of fibroblast expansion of LL and SL in the joints.
source: Additionally, Mir221/222 deletion in arthritis did not alter the inflammatory influx (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), but rather led to the inhibition of fibroblast expansion of LL and SL in the joints (Figure 5B).
evidence: This claim is supported by FACS analysis data shown in Figure 5B.

claim: Functional characterization of arthritic SFs in the absence of Mir221/222 showed decreased proliferative capacity than SFs from huTNFtg mice.
source: Ex vivo, functional characterization of arthritic SFs in the absence of Mir221/222 showed decreased proliferative capacity than SFs from huTNFtg mice (Figure 5C), confirming the control of cell proliferation by these two miRNAs.
evidence: This claim is supported by cell cycle analysis data shown in Figure 5C.

claim: Cdkn1b, Cdkn1c, and Smarca1 RNA and protein levels were partially restored in huTNFtg;Mir221/222-/- mice.
source: Cdkn1b, Cdkn1c, and Smarca1 RNA and protein levels were partially restored (Figure 5D–K), verifying their regulation by Mir221/222, although alternative or feedback mechanisms might also exist preventing the complete restoration of the expression levels of these genes and complete disease protection of huTNFtg;Mir221/222-/- mice.
evidence: This claim is supported by qRT-PCR and western blot data shown in Figure 5D–K.

claim: Combined transfection of HEK293 cells with pre-Mir221/222 and a plasmid carrying the Mir221/222 binding site of Smarca1 decreased luciferase activity.
source: As seen in Figure 5L, combined transfection of HEK293 cells with pre-Mir221/222 and a plasmid carrying the Mir221/222 binding site of Smarca1 decreased luciferase activity contrary to transfections with scramble pre-Mir and/or a plasmid carrying a mutated Mir221/222 binding site of Smarca1.
evidence: This claim is supported by luciferase assay data shown in Figure 5L.

claim: Smarca1 is a direct target of Mir221/222.
source: As seen in Figure 5L, combined transfection of HEK293 cells with pre-Mir221/222 and a plasmid carrying the Mir221/222 binding site of Smarca1 decreased luciferase activity contrary to transfections with scramble pre-Mir and/or a plasmid carrying a mutated Mir221/222 binding site of Smarca1.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the luciferase assay data shown in Figure 5L.

claim: Mir221/222 locus (Mirc53) is more accessible in the pathogenic intermediate and destructive lining clusters.
source: As can be seen, Mir221/222 locus (Mirc53) is more accessible in the pathogenic intermediate and destructive lining clusters (Figure 6B, Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C), marking their aberrant expansion.
evidence: This claim is supported by scATAC-seq data shown in Figure 6B and Figure 6—figure supplement 1B and C.

claim: Inferred linkages between accessible chromatin (peaks) and Mir221/222 genetic locus revealed transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs) of previously reported positive regulators such as Nfe2l2, Junb, Rela, Relb and Bach1 to be enriched in the regulatory regions associated with Mir221/222 locus.
source: Inferred linkages between accessible chromatin (peaks) and Mir221/222 genetic locus revealed transcription factor binding sites (TFBSs) of previously reported positive regulators such as Nfe2l2, Junb, Rela, Relb and Bach1 (Armaka et al., 2022), to be enriched in the regulatory regions associated with Mir221/222 locus (Figure 6C, Figure 6—figure supplement 1D).
evidence: This claim is supported by scATAC-seq data analysis shown in Figure 6C and Figure 6—figure supplement 1D.
